correction.title: Six CI workflows pin August 2026 sharp-runtime commits that lack components CNA's default closure requests (Xml.Serialization off Windows, Resources everywhere), so they stop at configure
correction.summary: CNA's default sharp-runtime component closure has requested Xml.Serialization on non-Windows targets since 2026-09-06 and Resources on every target since 2026-09-20. The workflows pinned to sharp-runtime bc8dbf41, f23ded28 or df1b42ab check out revisions that register neither, and sharp-runtime ends configuration with 'Unknown Sharp Runtime component'. The five non-Windows lanes have therefore failed at configure since 2026-09-06; only the Windows content-pipeline lane is broken solely by Resources.
correction.actual: cmake/SharpRuntimeConsumption.cmake lists Resources in CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_DEFAULT_COMPONENTS (added on 2026-09-20 for ResourceContentManager) and, off Windows, Xml.Serialization (added on 2026-09-06 for the math XmlSerializationEXT header). The root CMakeLists.txt passes that list as SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS before add_subdirectory of the sharp-runtime checkout, and merges every default component back into a cached or user-supplied SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS (FORCE), so no override can drop them. .github/workflows/htmldom-ci.yml, .github/workflows/devices-tests.yml and .github/workflows/emscripten-multi-renderer-ci.yml check out sharp-runtime bc8dbf41 (2026-08-15); .github/workflows/apple-ci.yml (both jobs) and .github/workflows/metal-macos-ci.yml f23ded28 (2026-08-15); .github/workflows/content-pipeline-windows-ci.yml df1b42ab (2026-08-28). None of the three revisions has modules/resources or modules/xml-serialization, and their cmake/SharpRuntimeComponents.cmake stops with FATAL_ERROR 'Unknown Sharp Runtime component' for an unregistered name. At this snapshot the configure error names Resources first on every lane, because Resources precedes Xml.Serialization in the closure; before 2026-09-20 the non-Windows lanes already stopped on Xml.Serialization. CNA's own plans/plan_software.md records that Xml.Serialization is absent from sharp-runtime df1b42ab. Most other workflows clone a branch head through scripts/ci/clone_siblings.sh (the pushed or pull-request branch when sharp-runtime has it, otherwise next); .github/workflows/d3d-windows-ci.yml and .github/workflows/gdi-windows-ci.yml (manual dispatch only) check out sharp-runtime's default branch with actions/checkout and no ref. Apart from the six pins, the snapshot records no sharp-runtime revision.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading the workflows and CMake files at 009d40f5, and the three sharp-runtime revisions (tree listing and cmake/SharpRuntimeComponents.cmake) in the local sharp-runtime checkout; nothing executed, and no CI run results are part of the snapshot. The Resources addition is CNA commit 8c1c8b412 (2026-09-20); Xml.Serialization joined the closure in CNA commit 0794128b6 (2026-09-06), and CNA's own plans/plan_software.md records that Xml.Serialization is absent from sharp-runtime df1b42ab. In the local sharp-runtime checkout, main (last commit 2026-08-22) and develop (df1b42ab) register neither component while next registers both; what GitHub's default branch held when the two manual Windows lanes would be dispatched is not recorded in the snapshot.

correction.summary: scripts/check_no_posix_setenv.py forbids POSIX setenv/unsetenv under modules/, tools/ and tests/, but the native Wayland backend and its tests added twelve such lines on 2026-09-15 and 2026-09-16, so the gate CNA registers in every test-enabled tree has exited 1 since 2026-09-15.
correction.actual: scripts/check_no_posix_setenv.py reports twelve lines: ::unsetenv("XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN") in modules/platform/src/Wayland/WaylandPlatform.cpp, and setenv/unsetenv of WAYLAND_SOCKET, WAYLAND_DISPLAY, LC_ALL, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN in WaylandDesktopPortalTests.cpp, WaylandProtocolTests.cpp, WaylandTestCompositor.cpp and WaylandTestEnvironment.cpp, all under modules/platform/tests/CNA/Platform/. The test is added in modules/graphics-ext/examples/CMakeLists.txt inside if(CNA_BUILD_TESTS) whenever a Python 3 interpreter is found, so it is red in every test-enabled tree. The Wayland code never reaches a Windows build (modules/platform/CMakeLists.txt compiles src/Wayland only for CNA_PLATFORM=WAYLAND, and cmake/UnitTests.cmake drops the Wayland tests otherwise), so the MinGW breakage the gate guards against does not occur; the defect is the permanently red gate. .github/workflows/general-tests-ci.yml runs an unfiltered ctest and its known-failure list names only EasyGL_GraphicsDevice_ReferenceStencil, so that job would classify this failure as new.
correction.evidence_note: Executed: python3 scripts/check_no_posix_setenv.py . against the read-only extracted snapshot tree (a text scan, nothing built); it printed the twelve lines and exited 1, and the same scan repeated for this review gave the same result. CNA's own records agree: docs/opengl4-renderer.md lists CNAEXT_NoPosixSetenv as the one CNAEXT example failure "on every renderer", and several plans record it as a standing failure. The first Wayland lines arrived in commits 678c6a51b and 227157d2c (2026-09-15) and the last four in c6e125083 and a271ae0ef (2026-09-16), all after the gate (c9f1359e1, 2026-08-19). Not executed: ctest itself or any CI run.

refutation_attempt: Traced the second call after a failed create_directories through EnsureStorageRoot, StorageContainer's ctor, DeleteContainer/ResolveContainedPath and LocalGamerServicesStore::StoreRoot, looking for an empty-root guard or retry; none exists. Checked CNA-BUG-150: a different defect (unsynchronised race), not a duplicate.
reason: The flag is set before the root is computed, so after a failed create_directories every later call returns an empty root; ResolveContainedPath treats an empty base as '.', so EndOpenContainer and DeleteContainer act in the working directory and the space/connection properties report LLONG_MAX/false. Reachable in unwritable-HOME containers; medium fits.
read: modules/storage/src/StorageDevice.cpp::EnsureStorageRoot, SetAppNameEXT, GetStorageRootEXT, DeleteContainer, EndOpenContainer, getIsConnectedProperty, getFreeSpaceProperty, getTotalSpaceProperty

refutation_attempt: Checked the terminal mouse really exists: GetMouse returns a TerminalMouse when canQuery, which is only isatty(stdin) after isatty(stdout), not a terminal reply. Looked for a catch in Game, a capability gate, a Game-level terminal test and a doc calling the throw intended: none.
reason: Reachable: the Game base constructor already creates the terminal window, and any interactive TTY session gets a TerminalMouse whose SetCursorVisible throws, contradicting PLAT-49 ('no-op under TERMINAL') and the XNA setter. But the trigger is misdescribed: canQuery is isatty(stdin), not a capability answer, so every interactive terminal is hit, not only ones that answer queries.

correction.summary: Game::setIsMouseVisibleProperty forwards to IPlatformMouse::SetCursorVisible whenever a window and a mouse service exist; the terminal platform supplies a TerminalMouse whenever stdin and stdout are both terminals (TerminalCapabilities::canQuery is isatty(stdin), independent of whether the emulator answers any query), and that mouse always throws.
correction.actual: Game::setIsMouseVisibleProperty records the value and then, when GraphicsDevice_ has a platform window and platform_->GetMouse() is non-null, calls SetCursorVisible(value). On the terminal platform the window exists only for the SOFTWARE renderer (the one family that asks for a surface presenter) on a TTY; GraphicsDevice creates it during Game construction. TerminalPlatform::GetMouse() runs EnsureCapabilitiesDetected, which creates a TerminalMouse whenever DetectTerminalCapabilities reports canQuery; canQuery is isatty(stdin) on top of isatty(stdout) and is set before any query is sent, so every interactive terminal session gets the mouse, whether or not the emulator answers the capability queries or supports mouse reporting. TerminalMouse::SetCursorVisible unconditionally throws PlatformException (a terminal cannot control its emulator's graphical pointer). The setter does not catch it, so IsMouseVisible = true in a game's constructor ends construction in an interactive terminal. With stdin or stdout redirected there is no mouse service (and, for stdout, no window), and the call is a no-op. CNA's own plans/plan_platform.md PLAT-49 records that IsMouseVisible was meant to be a determinate no-op under HEADLESS and, later, TERMINAL; PLAT-139 later gave the terminal mouse a service that refuses visibility changes.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading Game.cpp, TerminalMouse.cpp, TerminalPlatform.cpp, TerminalCapabilityProbe.cpp, IPlatformMouse.hpp and the tests at 009d40f5; not executed, no terminal session was driven. TerminalCapabilityProbeTests (ATerminalThatAnswersNothingLeavesEveryQueriedCapabilityFalse) pins that canQuery stays true when the terminal answers nothing. The test's premise (headless and, later, terminal both take the no-pointer path) holds only when stdin or stdout is not a terminal, as under ctest, which is why it passes. TerminalMouseTests pins the platform-level refusal, so what is missing is the caller's handling of it, not the refusal itself.

refutation_attempt: Searched for external Dispose(bool) callers (modules, tests, C API), a non-final subclass needing public access, and any intent comment: none; the four classes are final. Re-read each !disposing branch and the subsystem's raw owner pointer: cleanup skipped, registration dangles for Accelerometer and Gyroscope.
reason: Real as described: all four override Dispose(bool) publicly, Dispose(false) only sets disposed_, the destructor then skips cleanup, and a started Accelerometer/Gyroscope leaves a dangling registration. Severity lowered to low: exposure needs a deliberate external Dispose(false), which ported XNA/WP code cannot contain (protected there) and no CNA code or test calls.

refutation_attempt: Grepped every module for readers of FNA_KEYBOARD_USE_SCANCODES (only SdlInputBridge.cpp), traced who reads the legacy InputManager held-key set (text input only), and re-read FNA's ToXNAKey and GetKeyFromScancode locally. Git shows GetState used InputManager, and so honoured the mode, until PLAT-79 on 2026-08-13.
reason: Re-derived: Keyboard::GetState copies the platform snapshot, whose SDL3 service resolves held scancodes through the current layout, while GetKeyFromScancodeEXT becomes identity in scancode mode, so the halves disagree and the documented layout-independent mode does not reach GetState. A regression from PLAT-79; opt-in but documented, so medium.

refutation_attempt: Grepped all non-test code for RegisterForWindow: the four renderers never call it, GraphicsDevice does not register for them, and Mouse and the input bridge look renderers up only through GetForWindow. Read all four transforms (real, not stubs); history shows none ever registered.
reason: Re-derived: the transforms exist (DX11/DX12 added by DX-217 on 2026-09-08) but nothing registers them, so GetForWindow returns null and Mouse::GetState, SetPosition and touch pass raw window coordinates, against the registry's stated rule. Wrong only when window and back buffer differ (resize, letterbox, fullscreen, scale); medium fits.
